title: The Crooked Sigil Anew
premise: Elodie Yarrow has survived a decade by selling harmless trinkets in Vellharrow, a city where the guilds that once wove real magic were purged and their survivors forced into silence. When a mute child appears at her shop speaking the First Tongue—the language that predates kingdoms and binds the covenant between the human realm and the fading Otherworld—Elodie realizes the child is a living key, and that hunters from both realms want her. To protect the girl, Elodie must gather the scattered remnants of her guild, confront the corrupt magistrate who outlawed magic to hoard its power for himself, and reforge the broken covenant before the veil collapses entirely. In the end, Elodie sacrifices her own name and memories—her very identity—to seal the new sigil, saving both realms but becoming a stranger even to herself, remembered only by the child she saved.
about_author: Sable Voss is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing suppressed grimoires in private collections before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about people who survive by staying small, and what happens when smallness finally fails.

chapters.title: Charms Without Teeth
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A day in her charm shop: hollow trinkets sold to superstitious buyers while guild-inspectors patrol the street. We learn the purge of the Weaver's Guild ten years ago took her mentor and her confidence. Emotional beat: weary invisibility, the ache of unused talent.

chapters.title: The Child at the Door
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. On a rain-lashed night, a mute girl arrives speaking words that make Elodie's dormant sigil-marks burn. The child carries an old guild token belonging to Elodie's dead mentor. Emotional beat: terror and recognition colliding.

chapters.title: What the Inspectors Burn
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Guild-inspectors raid neighboring shops; Elodie hides the child beneath her floorboards among contraband charms. She learns the magistrate Corvane has posted a reward for 'a girl of strange speech.' Emotional beat: fear hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: First Tongue
chapters.summary: The child's POV (rendered through Elodie's attempts to understand). Through drawings and dream-echoes, we learn the girl fled the Otherworld as the veil thinned, carrying a fragment of the covenant-sigil inside her. Emotional beat: loneliness finding its first bridge.

chapters.title: The Last of the Guild
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. She seeks out Bren, a disgraced guild-scribe now drinking himself blind in the dockside quarter, and Tammas, a charm-maker turned blacksmith. Reluctantly, they agree the child must be protected. Emotional beat: guilt over a decade of silence.

chapters.title: Corvane's Ledger
chapters.summary: Magistrate Corvane's POV. We see his cold calculus: he outlawed magic not from piety but to monopolize it, siphoning covenant-power through hidden conduits to extend his life. He learns the child exists. Emotional beat: patient, rotting ambition.

chapters.title: Smoke Over Tanner's Row
chapters.summary: Bren's POV. Inspectors torch a safehouse; the group scatters into the undercity tunnels. Bren reveals the guild kept a second sigil-stone, hidden in the drowned chapel beyond the walls. Emotional beat: camaraderie forged in flight.

chapters.title: The Drowned Chapel
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. In a flooded ruin, they recover the sigil-stone, but touching it floods Elodie with her mentor's final memories—including his warning that reforging the covenant demands a life freely given. Emotional beat: grief as inheritance.

chapters.title: A Bargain in the Undercity
chapters.summary: Tammas's POV. To move unseen, they bargain with the Veiled Market, a smuggler network run by half-blooded Others stranded when the veil closed. Their price: a favor owed, unnamed. Emotional beat: uneasy alliance across old wounds.

chapters.title: Hunters of Both Realms
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Corvane's hunters and an Otherworld warden named Serevan both close in. Serevan captures the child briefly; Elodie trades her mentor's token to buy her back. Emotional beat: the first true cost of choosing sides.

chapters.title: Serevan's Grief
chapters.summary: Serevan's POV. The warden's own realm is dying because the covenant broke; he hunts the child believing returning her will restore it. He begins to doubt whether either side can be trusted with her. Emotional beat: duty cracking against conscience.

chapters.title: The Name in the Wall
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Hidden in the guild's old meetinghouse, they find the covenant's original terms: the Weaver's Guild were not mages but mediators, and every renewal required a willing sacrifice of selfhood. Elodie understands why her mentor hid this. Emotional beat: dread of the truth long buried.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Veiled Market
chapters.summary: Tammas's POV. Corvane buys the smugglers' debt; the market turns on them. Tammas holds the tunnel collapse so the others escape, and is taken alive. Emotional beat: sacrifice without applause.

chapters.title: What Corvane Offers
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. He interrogates Tammas, then sends an offer to Elodie: the child's life spared if she delivers the sigil-stone. He genuinely believes only he can manage the covenant safely. Emotional beat: corruption dressed as stewardship.

chapters.title: The Child Chooses
chapters.summary: The child's POV. Having learned enough human speech, the girl speaks her first words: she knows what the covenant requires, and she offers herself. Elodie refuses to let a child pay for adults' failures. Emotional beat: fierce, protective love.

chapters.title: Storming the Spire
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. With Bren, Serevan, and the freed smugglers, they assault Corvane's spire where the stolen conduit-power pools. Tammas is rescued mid-battle; the city watches magic burn openly for the first time in a decade. Emotional beat: hope kindled in open rebellion.

chapters.title: The Conduit Breaks
chapters.summary: Bren's POV. They shatter Corvane's siphons, but the released power tears the veil wider—Otherworld creatures spill into Vellharrow as the sky splits. Corvane, desperate, seizes the child. Emotional beat: victory curdling into catastrophe.

chapters.title: Two Kings of Nothing
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Confrontation atop the spire: Corvane wants to rule one realm; Serevan's superiors want to abandon the other. Elodie declares a third path—renewal on her own terms. Emotional beat: defiance crystallizing into purpose.

chapters.title: The Reforging
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. At the veil's wound, Elodie begins the rite, offering her name, memories, and identity as the willing sacrifice. The child and the gathered remnants of the guild anchor the new sigil together. Emotional beat: transcendence through surrender.

chapters.title: What Remains of Elodie Yarrow
chapters.summary: The child's POV. The covenant seals; the veil heals into a permeable boundary rather than a wall. Corvane, stripped of his stolen power, ages into an ordinary man awaiting trial. But Elodie stands blank-eyed, knowing no one. Emotional beat: triumph shadowed by loss.

chapters.title: A Stranger in Her Own Shop
chapters.summary: Bren's POV. The city rebuilds with open, mediated magic; the guild re-forms around the child as its first new member. Bren and Tammas care for the woman who was Elodie, telling her stories of herself. Emotional beat: tenderness toward the unremembered.

chapters.title: The First Word Again
chapters.summary: The child's POV. Months later, the nameless woman tends the reopened charm shop. The child takes her hand and speaks in the First Tongue—and something in the woman answers, a flicker of the old sigil warming under her skin. Some selves cannot be fully erased. Emotional beat: quiet, earned hope.
